blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Self-consistency (SC) is a widely used decoding strategy for improving chain-of-thought reasoning, but it requires sampling many complete reasoning trajectories with a preset budget. Its efficient variants reduce the cost mainly by stopping full-trajectory sampling early or distributing the number of samples across questions. In this paper, we propose StepBack, a step-level error-localized resampling method for efficient test-time reasoning. Given a small set of draft trajectories, StepBack localizes likely first error positions using lightweight signals and then resamples the detected error step and its suffix, followed by majority answer voting. Empirically, StepBack matches the accuracy of SC on average across seven mathematical reasoning and multi-hop QA benchmarks, while reducing token usage by up to 41.26%. In addition, by nature, StepBack can be combined with adaptive inference methods such as Adaptive Consistency, further improving their inference-time efficiency.
blocks.zh: 自我一致性(SC)是一种被广泛使用的用于改进思维链推理的解码策略,但它需要用预先设定的预算来取样许多完整的推理轨迹. 其高效的变体主要通过提前停止全轨采样或将样本数量分散到各个问题来降低成本. 在本文中,我们提出了StepBack,一种步级误差本地化的重样方法,用于高效的测试时间推理. 考虑到少量的草稿轨迹,StepBack使用轻量级信号将可能的第一个错误位置本地化,然后重新标出检测到的错误步骤及其后缀,然后多数回答投票. 经验中,StepBack在7个数学推理和多跳QA基准中平均匹配SC的精度,同时将符号使用率减少高达41.26%. 此外,从性质上讲,StepBack可以与适应性一致性等适应性推论方法结合,进一步提高其推论时间效率.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Figure 1: StepBack achieves higher accuracy with significantly fewer generated tokens than self-consistency on GSM8K.
blocks.zh: 图1:StepBack在GSM8K上实现更高的精度,生成的令牌明显少于自我一致性.

blocks.en: Chain-of-thought prompting improves the reasoning ability of large language models (LLMs) ( Brown et al., 2020 ) by encouraging language models to verbalize intermediate steps before producing a final answer ( Wei et al., 2022 ; Kojima et al., 2022 ) . A widely used approach to further improve accuracy is Self-Consistency (SC), which samples multiple “complete” reasoning trajectories and selects the most frequent final answer ( Wang et al., 2022 ) . Despite its effectiveness, SC is computationally expensive: each additional candidate answer requires generating an entire reasoning trajectory from scratch, so the token cost grows linearly with both the number of sampled trajectories and the length of each trajectory.
blocks.zh: 通过鼓励语言模型在生成最终答案之前将中间步骤口头化(Wei等人,2022年;Kojima等人,2022年)。 一个被广泛使用的进一步提高准确性的方法是"自我一致性"(SC),该方法对多个"完整的"推理轨迹进行抽样,并选择最频繁的最终答案(Wang等人,2022年). 尽管其有效性,SC的计算成本是昂贵的:每个额外的候选答案需要从零开始生成一个整个推理轨迹,因此信使成本随抽样轨迹的数量和每个轨迹的长度而呈线性增长.

blocks.en: Figure 2: Instead of regenerating many full trajectories, StepBack identifies a likely first error step, reuses valid early steps, and resamples only the erroneous step and its suffix before majority voting with the same voting budget (32 in this example).
blocks.zh: 图2:StepBack没有重新生成许多完整的轨迹,而是识别出一个可能的第一个错误步骤,重新使用有效的早期步骤,在以相同的表决预算进行多数表决之前只重印错误步骤及其后缀(本例为32个).

blocks.en: Recent studies have sought to reduce this cost by adjusting the number of full trajectories to sample. Adaptive-Consistency (AC) and Early-Stopping Self-Consistency (ESC) stop sampling once sufficient answer agreement is observed; Difficulty-Adaptive Self-Consistency (DSC) allocates larger budgets to harder questions; Reasoning-Aware Self-Consistency (RASC) makes stopping and voting more selective with rationale features ( Aggarwal et al., 2023 ; Li et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2025 ; Wan et al., 2025 ) . These methods improve decisions on when to stop sampling or how many trajectories to sample, but they largely operate at the level of complete trajectories. As a result, they leave open a finer-grained question: where to efficiently spend additional sampling within a reasoning trajectory?
blocks.zh: 最近的研究试图通过将全轨数调整为样本来降低这一成本. 适应性-一致性(AC)和早期停止自适性(ESC)一旦遵守了充分的答案协议就停止采样; 困难-自适性(DSC)将更大的预算分配给更困难的问题; 理性-智能自适性(RASC)使停止和投票更具选择性,具有理由特征(Aggarwal等人,2023年;Li等人,2024年;Wang等人,2025年;Wan等人,2025年)。 这些方法改进了对何时停止采样或采样时有多少轨迹的决定,但它们基本上在完全的轨迹水平上运作. 因此,它们留下了一个更细微的问题:在推理轨迹中如何有效地花费更多的采样?

blocks.en: This question is important because reasoning failures often emerge at an intermediate reasoning step rather than at only the final answer ( Wei et al., 2022 ; Uesato et al., 2022 ; Lightman et al., 2024 ) . Once such an error occurs, subsequent steps may hinge on the corrupted reasoning state, causing the error to propagate and end up with an incorrect final answer, a phenomenon also noted in prior work on accumulated errors in chain-of-thought reasoning ( Ling et al., 2023 ; Ouyang et al., 2026 ) . Meanwhile, the early steps of a reasoning chain contain useful problem setup ( Ji et al., 2025 ) . This suggests a sensible opportunity for efficient test-time reasoning: if a likely first erroneous step can be localized, the valid early steps can be preserved while only the erroneous step and its subsequent suffixes are resampled ( Tyen et al., 2024 ) .
blocks.zh: 这个问题很重要,因为推理失败往往出现在中间推理阶段,而不是仅仅出现在最后的答案(Wei等人,2022年;Uesato等人,2022年;Lightman等人,2024年). 一旦发生这种错误,随后的步骤可能取决于腐败的推理状态,导致错误传播,最终得到不正确的最终答案,这一现象也在先前关于思维链推理累积错误的著作中有所提及(Ling等人,2023年;Ouyang等人,2026年)。 同时,推理链的早期步骤包含了有用的问题设置(Ji等人,2025年). 这为高效的测试时间推理提供了合理的机会:如果一个可能的第一个错误步骤可以局部化,那么有效的早期步骤可以保留,而只有错误的步骤及其后续的后缀被重新标注(Tyen等人,2024年).

blocks.en: With this motivation, we propose StepBack , a step-level error-localized resampling method for efficient self-consistent reasoning. StepBack first generates a small set of draft trajectories and decomposes each trajectory into reasoning steps. It then uses lightweight signals, such as step-level negative log-likelihood, to localize likely first error positions. For each localized trajectory, StepBack reuses the earlier steps before the detected error, rolls back to the error step, and resamples the detected error step together with its suffixes. When no explicit error is detected, StepBack samples only the final answer step. The resulting candidate answers are then aggregated by majority voting, following the standard SC. This approach significantly cuts token usage while matching SC’s accuracy on average, as depicted in Figure 1 . The key contributions of our work are:
blocks.zh: 以此为动机,我们提出StepBack,一种步级误差本地化的复刻方法,用于高效的自我一致推理. StepBack首先生成一组小的草稿轨迹,并将每个轨迹分解为推理步骤. 然后它使用轻量级信号,如阶梯级负对数类似,将可能的第一个错误位置本地化. 对于每个本地化的轨迹,StepBack重用检测出错误之前的早期步骤,向后滚回错误步骤,再将检测出的错误步骤与它的后缀一起重印. 当未检测到明显错误时,StepBack只对最后的答案步骤进行抽样. 由此产生的候选人答复随后按照标准SC按多数票汇总。 如图1所示,这种做法在平均匹配SC准确性的同时大大削减了象征性的使用。 我们工作的主要贡献是:

blocks.en: • We introduce StepBack , an efficient step-level error-localized resampling method that reuses draft early steps, localizes likely first error positions with lightweight signals, and performs suffix resampling instead of repeated full-trajectory generation. • To the best of our knowledge, StepBack is the first self-consistency-based decoding method that uses step-level error localization to decide where to begin resampling, rather than sampling every candidate as a full trajectory. • We empirically show across mathematical reasoning and multi-hop QA benchmarks that StepBack can match or surpass full self-consistency while using substantially fewer generation tokens. We further show that StepBack can be seamlessly combined with adaptive inference methods such as Adaptive Consistency, Early-Stopping SC, and Difficulty-Adaptive SC.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Recent work reduces self-consistency cost by adaptively controlling the number of full trajectories to sample. Adaptive-Consistency stops once answer agreement is sufficient ( Aggarwal et al., 2023 ) ; Early-Stopping Self-Consistency uses simple window-based stopping rules ( Li et al., 2024 ) ; Reasoning-Aware Self-Consistency incorporates rationale-quality features into stopping and voting ( Wan et al., 2025 ) ; and Difficulty-Adaptive Self-Consistency allocates larger budgets to harder questions ( Wang et al., 2025 ) . These methods improve sampling efficiency by deciding how many trajectories to generate. In contrast, StepBack solves the problem where additional computation should be spent inside a trajectory. Thus, StepBack is complementary to adaptive SC methods: they reduce the number of consumed candidates, while StepBack reduces the cost of each candidate.
blocks.zh: 最近的工作通过适应性地控制采样的全轨距数量来降低自我一致性成本. 适应性-一致性一旦同意就停止(Aggarwal等人,2023年) ; 早期停止自我一致性使用简单的基于窗口的停止规则(Li等人,2024年) ; 理性-智能自我一致性将理性-质量特征纳入停止和投票(Wan等人,2025年) ; 困难-自主一致性将更大的预算分配给更难的问题(Wang等人,2025年). 这些方法通过决定产生多少轨迹来提高采样效率. 相比之下,StepBack解决了在轨迹内应花费额外计算的问题. 因此,StepBack是对适应性的SC方法的补充:它们减少了被消耗的候选者数量,而StepBack则减少了每个候选者的成本.

blocks.en: Process supervision and step-level verification show that intermediate reasoning steps carry useful signals about solution quality ( Uesato et al., 2022 ; Lightman et al., 2024 ) . Errors tend to propagate once an early step becomes invalid ( Ling et al., 2023 ) , early prefixes often contain reusable problem setup ( Ji et al., 2025 ) , and LLMs correct reasoning more effectively when the error location is given ( Tyen et al., 2024 ) . Several methods act on such signals by returning to an earlier step and regenerating from there: LeCo ( Yao et al., 2024 ) restarts after the lowest-confidence step until two consecutive answers agree; Singh et al. (2025) backtrack with a step-level verifier conditioned on previously attempted revisions; Adaptive Rectification Sampling ( Tan et al., 2025 ) prompts the model to rethink a step whose PRM score falls below a threshold; Thought Rollback ( Chen and Li, 2024 ) rolls back to earlier thoughts after analyzing their errors; and Self-Backtracking ( Yang et al., 2026 ) trains the model itself to decide when and where to backtrack. In these methods, each rollback depends on the outcome of earlier attempts, so revisions run sequentially and their total cost is not fixed in advance. StepBack instead uses lightweight signals, such as a negative log-likelihood increase or a process-reward score drop, to assign a single rollback point to each independent draft, so all suffix continuations can be generated in parallel and the number of candidate answers is fixed at B = n d ​ n s B=n_{d}n_{s} , the same budget as full-trajectory self-consistency. Each additional candidate reuses its draft prefix and therefore costs fewer tokens than a full trajectory, and StepBack requires no training and aggregates answers by standard majority voting.
blocks.zh: 过程监督和阶梯级核查显示,中间推理步骤带有关于溶液质量的有用信号(Uesato等人,2022年;Lightman等人,2024年). 一旦早期步骤无效,错误往往会传播(Ling等人,2023年),早期前缀往往包含可重复使用的问题设置(Ji等人,2025年),在给出错误位置时,LLMs会更有效地纠正推理(Tyen等人,2024年). 几种方法通过返回到更早的一步并从中再生,对这种信号采取行动: LeCo(Yao等人,2024年)在信心最低的一步后重启,直到连续两次回答达成一致;Singh等人(2025年)在此前尝试的修改中附带了阶梯级验证符;适应性校正抽样(Tan等人,2025年)促使模型重新考虑PRM得分低于阈值的一步;思想回滚(Chen和Li,2024年)在分析错误后回滚到更早的思考;以及自我回转(Yang等人,2026年)训练模型自己决定回转的时间和地点. 在这些方法中,每次回滚都取决于先前尝试的结果,因此修改是按顺序进行的,其总成本不事先固定. StepBack转而使用轻量级信号,如负的对数型的加分或过程-奖励分数的降分,为每个独立草稿分配一个单回滚点,因此所有后缀续作可以平行生成,候选答题数固定在B=nd n S B=n_{d}n_{s},预算与全导自相容性相同. 每个额外的候选人都会重新使用其草稿前缀,因此比整个轨迹花费更少的代币,StepBack不需要经过标准多数投票的培训和汇总答案.

blocks.en: 4.2 Comparison with Self-Consistency
blocks.zh: 4.2 与自我一致性的比较

blocks.en: Standard self-consistency (SC) samples B B complete reasoning trajectories from p θ ( ⋅ ∣ x ) p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x) and returns the majority normalized answer ( Wang et al., 2022 ) . Under the same answer budget, SC spends all samples on independent full trajectories, whereas StepBack spends the budget on repairing or diversifying uncertain suffixes of a smaller set of draft anchors. This allows StepBack to reuse reliable early steps while focusing additional sampling on steps that are more likely to affect the final answer, as illustrated in Fig. 2 .
blocks.zh: 标准自相容性(SC)样本 B B 完整推理轨迹出自p (⋅ ∣) p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x),并返回多数常态化的答案(Wang等人,2022年). 在同一解答预算下,SC将所有样本都用于独立的全轨,而StepBack则将预算用于修复或使一组较小的草稿锚的不确定后缀多样化. 这使StepBack能够重新利用可靠的早期步骤,同时将更多的取样集中在更可能影响到最后答案的步骤上,如图2所示。

blocks.en: 5 Experiments
blocks.zh: 5 实验

blocks.en: We evaluate whether StepBack can outperform or achieve a comparable performance to full-trajectory self-consistency (SC) at a fixed candidate-answer budget while reducing generation cost. The results focus on budget B = 32 B=32 and compare rollback-resampling against Greedy@1 and SC@32.
blocks.zh: 我们评价StepBack是否能够在固定的应答预算下,在降低生成成本的同时,取得与完全弹射自一贯性(SC)相似的业绩。 结果侧重于预算B=32 B=32,并将回滚抽样与Greedy@1和SC@32进行比较。

blocks.en: 5.1 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 5.1 实验设置

blocks.en:
We evaluate mathematical reasoning on GSM8K ( Cobbe et al., 2021 ) , MATH500 ( Hendrycks et al., 2021 ) , AMC2023, AIME24, and OlympiadBench ( He et al., 2024 ) , covering tasks from grade-school arithmetic to competition-level mathematics.
We further evaluate multi-hop question answering on HotpotQA ( Yang et al., 2018 ) and 2WikiMultiHopQA ( Ho et al., 2020 ) , which require composing evidence across multiple supporting facts.
For efficiency, we randomly sample 500 examples from the HotpotQA validation set of 7,405 examples and 1,000 examples from the 2WikiMultiHopQA validation set of 12.6K examples.
blocks.zh:
我们评价GSM8K(Cobbe等人,2021年),MATH500(Hendrycks等人,2021年),AMC2023,AIME24,和Olympiad Bench(He等人,2024年)的数学推理,涵盖从年级算术到竞赛级数学的任务.
我们进一步评价对HotpotQA(Yang等人,2018年)和2Wiki MultiHopQA(Ho等人,2020年)的多跳问题回答,这需要跨越多个佐证事实形成证据.
为了提高效率,我们随机抽取了HotpotQA验证集的500个实例,其中7,405个实例,以及2Wiki MultiHopQA验证集12.6K实例的1000个实例.

blocks.en: The model set contains Qwen-2.5-3B-Instruct , Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct , and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct . These models span various architectures and scales, allowing us to test whether error-localized suffix resampling is robust beyond a single backbone.
blocks.zh: 该型号集包含Quen-2.5-3B-Instruct ,Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct ,以及Quen-2.5-7B-Instruct . 这些模型跨越各种架构和尺度,使我们能够测试错误本地化的后缀复标是否超出一个主干线。

blocks.en: The primary baseline is self-consistency (SC) ( Wang et al., 2022 ) , which samples B = 32 B=32 complete chain-of-thought trajectories independently and selects the most frequent normalized final answer. We also report greedy chain-of-thought decoding (CoT), which generates one deterministic reasoning trajectory and serves as a low-cost reference point. In Section 5.3 , we additionally compare against adaptive reasoning methods, including Adaptive Consistency (AC) ( Aggarwal et al., 2023 ) , Early-Stopping Self-Consistency (ESC) ( Li et al., 2024 ) , and Difficulty-Adaptive Self-Consistency (DSC) ( Wang et al., 2025 ) . Details for their hyperparameters can be found in Appendix J . For the main comparison, StepBack uses the same candidate-answer budget as SC@32. We consider two lightweight variants of the localization signal: NLL-signal and PRM-signal , both described in Section 4.1 .
blocks.zh: 主要基线为自相容性(SC)(Wang等人,2022年),其B = 32 B = 32 完整的思维链轨迹独立取样,并选择最常见的常态化最终答案. 我们还报告贪婪的思维链解码(CoT),它产生一个决定性的推理轨迹,并作为一个低成本的参考点。 在第5.3节中,我们进一步比较适应性推理方法,包括适应性一致性(AC)(Aggarwal等人,2023年),早期停止自适应性(ESC)(Li等人,2024年),以及困难自适应性(DSC)(Wang等人,2025年)。 其超参数的细节见附录J。 对于主要比较,StepBack使用与SC@32相同的候选人回答预算. 我们认为本地化信号有两个轻量级的变体:NLL信号和PRM信号,两者都在第4.1节中描述.

blocks.en:
Unless otherwise specified, we use thresholds 0.1 0.1 for NLL-signal and 0.05 0.05 for PRM-signal , without dataset-specific tuning.
Lower thresholds trigger a rollback on modest drops of the step-level signal, so more drafts are rewritten since an earlier step; this favors accuracy over token saving.
These thresholds are shared across all datasets and models; a held-out calibration on training questions (Appendix F ) shows that every threshold in a wide grid matches or exceeds the average accuracy of SC@32 while saving 20–44% of tokens.

On MATH500, it improves Qwen-3B, Llama-3B, and Qwen-7B by + 0.40 +0.40 , + 1.20 +1.20 , and + 2.00 +2.00 points while saving 25.60 % 25.60\% , 20.81 % 20.81\% , and 28.53 % 28.53\% tokens, respectively. Notably, although the PRM is trained primarily for mathematical process supervision, it also provides useful step-level reliability estimates for logical and multi-hop reasoning: on HotpotQA, PRM-signal improves Qwen-3B and Qwen-7B by + 1.20 +1.20 and + 2.20 +2.20 points but lowers Llama-3B by 2.00 2.00 points, which suggests that PRM-signal can capture some reasoning-quality drops beyond purely arithmetic errors, but less reliably than on mathematical reasoning.
blocks.zh: 每个数据集,PRM-信号会减少所有21个模型-数据集对(7.66–41.26%)生成的令牌,提高其中14个的准确度,1个带,6个带更低. 在MATH500上,它改进了Quen-3B,Llama-3B,以及Quen-7B,分别增加了+0.40+0.40,+1.20+1.20,以及+2.00+2.00分,同时节省了25.60%的25.60\%,20.81%的20.81%的20.81%的20.81\%,28.53%的28.53%的标志. 值得注意的是,虽然PRM主要接受数学过程监督的培训,但也为逻辑和多跳推理提供了有用的阶梯级可靠性估计:在HotpotQA上,PRM-信号将Quen-3B和Quen-7B改进为+1.20+1.20和+2.20+2.20分,但将Llama-3B降低2.02.00分,这表明PRM-信号可以捕捉一些纯算术误差之外的推理质量下降,但不如数学推理可靠.

blocks.en: Meanwhile, NLL-signal provides a complementary low-cost localization signal requiring no external model: it achieves larger token savings than PRM-signal on 17 of the 21 pairs and improves accuracy of Qwen-3B and Qwen-7B on two multi-hop QA datasets. We factor this in that NLL-signal tends to localize errors less aggressively, often rolling back closer to the final answer and therefore resampling shorter suffixes. This yields stronger token savings, but may leave more earlier reasoning errors unedited compared to PRM-signal .
blocks.zh: 同时,NLL-signal提供了补充的低成本本地化信号,不需要外部模型:它比21对中的17对PRM-signal实现了更大的代号节约,并且提高了两个多跳QA数据集上的Quen-3B和Quen-7B的精度. 我们考虑这一点,因为NLL-信号倾向于将错误定位得不那么积极,往往向后滚动更接近最后的答案,从而重印较短的后缀. 与PRM信号相比,

blocks.en: The additional cost of computing localization signals remains modest compared with the cost of generating complete reasoning trajectories. The relative localization overhead ρ 16 \rho_{16} in Table 2 , i.e., the share of the wall-clock time of StepBack spent scoring the drafts, averages 8.38 % 8.38\% , 9.52 % 9.52\% , and 10.93 % 10.93\% for NLL-signal and 7.48 % 7.48\% , 9.86 % 9.86\% , and 6.98 % 6.98\% for PRM-signal on Llama-3B, Qwen-3B, and Qwen-7B, respectively. Thus, the token savings achieved by StepBack are not offset by a large scoring cost.
blocks.zh: 与产生完整的推理轨迹相比,计算本地化信号的额外费用仍然不大。 表2的相对本地化管理费 $ 16\rho_{16},即StepBack的墙上时间占分数,平均为8.38% ,9.52% ,9.52 % ,10.93% 10.93 % NLL-信号和7.48% 7.48 % 9.86% 9.86 % , 6.98% PRM-标志在Llama-3B,Quen-3B和Quen-7B上分别使用. 因此,StepBack实现的象征性节余不会被巨额评分费用抵消。

blocks.en:
The gains of accuracy suggest that many incorrect draft trajectories are not entirely unhelpful since they often contain correct early steps. Instead of discarding these steps as SC does, StepBack keeps the reliable part of each draft and resamples only from the predicted error region.
This design is especially effective on datasets where errors often arise in later reasoning stages, such as GSM8K, MATH500, and AMC2023, where PRM-signal improves accuracy for all three models while saving 10.83–41.26% of generated tokens.
The consistent token reduction across all settings further indicates that localized resampling avoids a large amount of redundant early steps generation.
blocks.zh:
准确性的提高表明,许多不正确的轨道草案并非完全无益,因为它们往往包含正确的早期步骤。 StepBack没有像SC那样丢弃这些步骤,而是将每个草稿的可靠部分保留下来,只从预测的错误区域复制.
这种设计对数据集特别有效,在后期推理阶段经常出现错误,如GSM8K,MATH500,AMC2023,其中PRM-信号可以提高所有三种模型的精度,同时节省10.83–41.26%的生成令牌.
在所有设置中一致的代号减少进一步表明,本地化的重新取样可避免大量冗余的早期步骤生成.

blocks.en: On harder competition-style benchmarks such as AIME24 and OlympiadBench, the gains are less stable, especially for Llama-3B. This suggests that some failures cannot be corrected by resampling only a localized suffix, since they may require revising earlier reasoning decisions or exploring a substantially different solution path.
blocks.zh: 在AIME24和Olympiad Bench等较硬的竞争类基准上,收益的稳定性较低,对Llama-3B来说尤其如此。 这表明一些失败无法通过只重印本地化后缀来纠正,因为这些失败可能需要修改先前的推理决定或探索一个截然不同的解决方案路径.

blocks.en: Overall, these results support the central premise of StepBack : under a fixed answer budget, additional test-time compute can be spent more efficiently by resampling from a localized likely error step instead of regenerating every candidate from scratch.
blocks.zh: 总的来说,这些结果支持StepBack的中心前提:在固定的答案预算下,通过从局部可能的误差步骤中重新取样,而不是从零开始重新生成每个候选人,可以更有效地使用额外的测试时间计算。

blocks.en: 5.3 StepBack as a Complement to Adaptive Reasoning
blocks.zh: 5.3 后退作为适应性理由的补充

blocks.en:

For StepBack , the candidate pool is built from n d = 16 n_{d}=16 draft anchors and n s = 2 n_{s}=2 candidate answers per draft (the draft’s own answer and one localized suffix sample), using PRM-signal . CoT表示贪婪的思维链解码. 对于StepBack,候选人池由n d = 16 n_{d}=16 草稿主播和n s = 2 n_{s}=2 草稿候选人答案(草稿本身的答案和一个本地化的后缀样本)构建,使用PRM-信号. PExp(Jindal等人,2026年)是每个问题平均消耗的候选扩展数. 就SC/AC/ESC/DSC而言,每次扩展都是一个完整的轨道。 对于StepBack,每次扩展都是草稿轨迹或局部后缀续作. Tok.是每个问题生成的令牌数量,而G/1kT是每1k生成的令牌相对于CoT的精度增益.

blocks.en: Table 3 shows that StepBack can be directly combined with adaptive reasoning methods. AC, ESC, and DSC originally operate on a pool of independently generated full trajectories and decide how many candidates to consume. We instead replace this full-trajectory pool with the StepBack suffix pool: StepBack first generates draft anchors and localized suffix continuations, and the adaptive policy is then applied to these suffix candidates. Therefore, StepBack reduces the token cost of each candidate, while AC/ESC/DSC further reduces the number of consumed candidates.
blocks.zh: 表3显示StepBack可以直接与适应推理方法结合. AC,ESC,和DSC最初运行在一个独立生成的完整轨迹的集合上,并决定要消耗多少候选人. 我们用StepBack的后缀池取代了这个完全的弹射池: StepBack首先生成草稿主播和局部后缀续作,然后将这些适应政策应用于这些后缀候选人. 因此,StepBack减少了每个候选人的象征性费用,而AC/ESC/DSC则进一步减少了被消耗的候选人人数.

blocks.en: These two reductions compound. Relative to each adaptive method alone, adding StepBack cuts generated tokens by 22–24% on MATH500, 35–38% on GSM8K, and 6–7% on HotpotQA. Accuracy also improves in all six comparisons on GSM8K and HotpotQA, by 1.1–2.2 points, and G/1kT improves in all nine; on MATH500, accuracy is only 0.2–0.8 points lower. The most efficient combination, StepBack +DSC on GSM8K, uses 5.2 × \times fewer tokens than SC@32 while being 0.9 points more accurate.
blocks.zh: 这两个削减复合。 相对于每个适应性方法,在MATH500、GSM8K和HotpotQA各增加22–24 % 、 35–38% 和 6–7% 。 在GSM8K和HotpotQA的所有6个比较中,精确度也提高了1.1–2.2分,G/1kT在所有9个比较中都提高了;在MATH500上,精确度只有0.2-0.8分低. 最有效率的组合,即GSM8K上的StepBack + DSC,使用5.2×\time比SC@32少的代币,同时更准确0.9分.

blocks.en: Overall, the combination improves the accuracy-cost trade-off over both standard SC and adaptive reasoning alone, showing that StepBack is a complementary intra-trajectory allocation strategy rather than a replacement for adaptive inference.
blocks.zh: 总的来说,这种组合改进了准确性成本与标准SC和适应性推理的权衡,表明StepBack是一种互补的弹道内部分配策略,而不是替代适应性推论.

blocks.en: 6 Analysis and Discussions
blocks.zh: 6. 分析和讨论

blocks.en: Table 14 in Appendix H studies whether StepBack relies on a large PRM for error localization. We fix the generator to Qwen2.5-3B and evaluate on MATH500, comparing Skywork-o1-Open-PRM-Qwen-2.5-1.5B ( He et al., 2025 ) with Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B under the same B = 32 B=32 candidate-answer budget.
blocks.zh: 附录中的表14 H研究StepBack是否依赖于一个大PRM进行错误本地化. 我们把生成器修到 Quen2.5-3B 上,然后在 MATH500 上进行评估,比对 Skywork-o1-Open-PRM-Quen-2.5-1.5B (He等人,2025年)与Quen2.5-Math-PRM-7B在同一B=32B=32候选人回答预算下.

blocks.en: The results show that StepBack does not require a PRM larger than the generator. With the 1.5B Skywork PRM, StepBack still outperforms SC@32 in the 8 × 4 8\times 4 setting, improving accuracy by + 0.36 +0.36 points while saving 23.8 % 23.8\% generation tokens, although the accuracy is 0.36 0.36 points below SC@32 at 16 × 2 16\times 2 . The 7B Qwen PRM gives stronger localization and achieves a higher accuracy gain of + 0.72 +0.72 points at 16 × 2 16\times 2 , but 1.5B PRM already preserves a substantial portion of the benefit with lower scoring overhead (13.7ms vs. 19.7ms per draft sample).
blocks.zh: 结果显示,StepBack不需要比生成器更大的PRM. 有了1.5B Skywork PRM,StepBack在8×4 8\times 4的设置中仍然超越SC@32,提高了精度+0.36+0.36分,同时节省了23.8% 23.8%的生成令牌,尽管精度在16×2 16\times时低于SC@320.360.36分. 2,7B Quen PRM给予更强的本地化,并在16×2 16\times 2 实现更高的 + 0.72 的精度增益,但1.5B PRM已经保留了很大一部分收益,分数较低(每份样本13.7ms对19.7ms).

blocks.en: This suggests that the key requirement is not PRM scale, but whether the localization signal is informative. Even lightweight signals, such as NLL-signal or a smaller PRM, can support effective suffix resampling when they identify useful rollback points.
blocks.zh: 这表明关键要求不是PRM规模,而是本地化信号是否信息化. 即使是轻量级信号,如NLL信号或较小的PRM,在识别有用的回滚点时,也能支持有效的后缀复标.

blocks.en: Table 12 in Appendix H studies how to allocate the same candidate budget B = 32 B=32 between draft anchors and suffix samples. Suffix-heavy settings such as 1 × 32 1\times 32 and 2 × 16 2\times 16 save the most tokens and 2 × 16 2\times 16 attains the highest G/1kT on three out of the seven datasets, since many candidates share the same short early steps. However, they are less stable in accuracy because a small number of flawed draft prefixes can limit recovery.
blocks.zh: 附录中的表12 H研究如何在主播草稿和后缀样本之间分配相同的候选预算B=32B=32. 后缀-重置设置,如1×32 1\times 32和2×16 2\times 16 省下最多的符号,2×16 2\times 16 在7个数据集中的3个数据上获得最高的G/1kT,因为许多考生共享相同的短暂的早期步骤. 然而,由于少数有缺陷的草稿前缀可以限制回收,因此它们准确性不甚稳定.

blocks.en: Draft-heavy settings such as 8 × 4 8\times 4 and 16 × 2 16\times 2 are more robust because they provide more diverse reasoning prefixes. 8 × 4 8\times 4 improves over SC@32 on all five math benchmarks, and 16 × 2 16\times 2 improves on GSM8K, MATH500, AMC2023, AIME24, and HotpotQA and matches it on OlympiadBench, while still saving tokens. These exhibit that n d n_{d} and n s n_{s} control an accuracy-efficiency trade-off: suffix-heavy settings are more cost-oriented, whereas draft-heavy settings are more accuracy-oriented.
blocks.zh: 草稿重的设置,例如8×4 8\time 4和16×2 16\time 2,因为提供了更多样化的推理前缀,所以比较强健. 8×4 8\Times 4在全部5个数学基准上比SC@32有所改进,16×2 16\Times 2在GSM8K,MATH500,AMC2023,AIME24,和HotpotQA上有所改进,并在Olympiad Bench上与之匹配,同时仍然保存符号. 这些显示 n d n_{d} 和 n s_{s} 控制精度效率的权衡: 后缀重置设置更注重成本, 而草稿重置则更注重精度.

blocks.en: Any rule that maps a draft to a rollback point can serve as Loc \mathrm{Loc} in Algorithm 1 , including signal-free rules such as random, fixed-position, and final-step rollback, and PRM-based rules from prior backtracking methods ( Singh et al., 2025 ; Tan et al., 2025 ) . Appendix G compares them with drafting, suffix resampling, and majority voting held fixed. Prefix reuse and suffix resampling yield most of the token saving under any rule, and late rules such as final-step resampling are strong efficiency baselines; on HotpotQA, final-step resampling is both more accurate and cheaper than PRM-signal . Localization helps most when suffix samples dominate the vote: at 4 × 8 4\times 8 , PRM-signal is 2.06 points more accurate than final-step resampling over all seven datasets.
blocks.zh: 任何将草稿映射到回滚点的规则都可以作为算法1中的Loc\mathrm{Loc},包括无信号规则,如随机,固定位置,以及最后一步回滚,以及基于PRM的规则,来自先前的回转方法(Singh等人,2025年;Tan等人,2025年). 附 录 G将其与起草,后缀重印,多数投票固定. 前缀复用和后缀复用会在任何规则下产生大部分的代号节省,而后缀复用等规则是强大的效率基线;在HotpotQA上,最终复用既准确又便宜于PRM-signal . 当后缀样本主导投票时,本地化最有帮助:在4×8 4\times 8时,PRM-信号比所有7个数据集的最终步骤重印更准确2.06分.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
We presented StepBack , a step-level error-localized resampling method for efficient test-time reasoning. Instead of regenerating every candidate from scratch, StepBack keeps the reliable prefix of each draft and resamples only from a likely first error located by lightweight NLL-signal or PRM-signal . Across seven mathematical reasoning and multi-hop QA benchmarks and three models, StepBack matches the average accuracy of SC@32 under the same answer budget while generating up to 41.26% fewer tokens, and it further reduces the cost of adaptive methods such as AC, ESC, and DSC.
These results suggest that where test-time compute is spent within a trajectory is a useful axis of efficiency, complementary to deciding how many trajectories to sample.
blocks.zh:
我们提出了StepBack, 一种步骤级误差本地化的复刻方法, 用于高效的测试时间推理 。 StepBack没有从零重新生成每个候选人,而是只从轻量级的NLL-signal或PRM-signal发现的可能的首个错误中保留每个草稿的可靠前缀,并重印. 在7个数学推理和多跳QA基准和3个模型中,StepBack匹配相同答案预算下SC@32的平均精度,同时产生高达41.26%的代币,并进一步降低了AC,ESC,DSC等适应方法的成本.
这些结果表明,如果试验时间计算在轨迹内是有用的效率轴,对决定有多少轨迹进行取样起到补充作用。

blocks.en: 8 Limitations and Broader Impact
blocks.zh: 8 限制和更广泛的影响

blocks.en:
StepBack has limitations that leave room for future work. First, we
focus on two representative localization signals, NLL-signal and PRM-signal . Although they already show clear benefits, exploring a broader set of even lighter-weight signals may further improve the efficiency of StepBack . Second, our experiments mainly focus on mathematical reasoning and multi-hop question answering. While StepBack performs well in these settings, its generalizability to other domains such as code generation or long-context summarization remains to be further studied.
blocks.zh:
StepBack有局限性,为今后的工作留有余地. 首先,我们
专注于两个有代表性的本地化信号,NLL信号和PRM信号. 虽然它们已经显示出明显的效益,但探索一套更广泛的更轻的信号,可能会进一步提高StepBack的效率. 第二,我们的实验主要集中于数学推理和多跳问答. 虽然StepBack在这些环境中表现良好,但其对诸如代码生成或长文本汇总等其他领域的可概括性仍有待进一步研究。

blocks.en: More efficient reasoning can make stronger inferences accessible at a lower cost, which is a positive outcome for scientific and educational use. At the same time, cheaper reasoning can also make capable systems easier to deploy at scale. We therefore believe that research on efficient reasoning should ideally improve both performance and transparency about where the gains come from.
blocks.zh: 更高效的推理可以使更强的推论以更低的成本获得,这是科学和教育使用的一个积极成果. 同时,更便宜的推理还可以使有能力的系统更容易大规模部署. 因此,我们认为,对有效推理的研究最好能够提高业绩,提高收益来源的透明度。

blocks.en: In this section, we evaluate whether lightweight signals can approximate the oracle first-error positions used in Section 3.2 . For each incorrect trajectory, we have an annotated first-error position e e . Given a localization signal, we predict a first-error position e ^ \hat{e} and compare it against e e . We also include a baseline, Random , that samples a rollback position randomly from the available reasoning steps in the trajectory. This baseline tests whether the signal-based methods do better than selecting a resampling point without using any information from the trajectory.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们评价轻量级信号是否可以大致显示第3.2节中使用的甲骨文第一偏差位置。 对于每一个不正确的轨迹,我们有一个附加注释的第一误差位置e。 鉴于一个本地化信号,我们预测一个第一误差位置 e ^\ hat{e} 并将其与 e 相比较 。 我们还包括一个基线 Random 从轨迹中的现有推理步骤随机抽取回滚位置 这种基线测试以信号为基础的方法是否比不使用轨迹中的任何信息而选择再模拟点更好。

blocks.en: For each trajectory with annotated first-error position e e , we evaluate the predicted position e ^ \hat{e} using the following four metrics.

blocks.en: Prev-1 measures whether the predicted position is either the annotated first-error step or the immediately preceding step: e ^ ∈ { max ⁡ ( 1 , e − 1 ) , e } . \hat{e}\in\{\max(1,e-1),e\}. (14) This metric captures whether the predicted resampling point is close enough to cover the first error while avoiding substantial wasted computation on already-correct early reasoning steps. When e ^ = e \hat{e}=e , resampling starts exactly at the first error; when e ^ = e − 1 \hat{e}=e-1 , only one additional valid step is resampled.

(15) This metric is important because resampling from a position before or at the true first error includes the erroneous step in the resampled suffix. However, it should be interpreted together with pre-error distance: a very early prediction can satisfy Not-Later while wasting computation by resampling many already-correct early reasoning steps. blocks.en: Table 5 shows that both lightweight signals contain information about where reasoning first becomes unreliable. PRM-signal with a threshold of δ = \delta= 0.05 achieves the best Exact and Prev-1 scores. For the same threshold, 52.3 % 52.3\% Not-Later rate indicates that the predicted point often falls no later than the annotated first-error step, making it possible to rewrite the erroneous step itself. Meanwhile, its Mean Pre-Error Distance remains at only 1.07 1.07 , explaining that it typically wastes about one correct step on average. This shows that an external process-level scorer can identify local reasoning degradation more accurately and place the resampling point close to the oracle first error without excessive early resampling. NLL-signal is weaker than PRM-signal , but still outperforms the Random baseline in all metrics except for Not-Later, exhibiting that sudden increases in token-level uncertainty may also provide a meaningful, though less precise, signal of reasoning failure.

NLL-信号比PRM-信号弱,但除Not-Late外,在所有的度量中仍然比Random基线表现优于Random基线,这表明表示值级不确定性的突然增加也可能提供有意义的,虽然不太精确的推理失败信号.

blocks.en: The main experiments use a single threshold per signal for all datasets and models, δ NLL = 0.1 \delta_{\mathrm{NLL}}=0.1 and δ PRM = 0.05 \delta_{\mathrm{PRM}}=0.05 . To examine how sensitive StepBack is to this choice, we calibrate both thresholds on held-out training questions.

blocks.en: We sample 100 questions from the MATH training set [ Hendrycks et al., 2021 ] and 100 from the HotpotQA training set [ Yang et al., 2018 ] . We run StepBack with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct in the 16 × 2 16\times 2 setting under two random seeds and sweep each threshold over the grid in Table 7 . Each threshold is scored by the macro average of MATH and HotpotQA accuracy, and the highest-scoring threshold is selected, with ties broken in favor of fewer generated tokens.

On this held-out set, the defaults match MATH accuracy at the SC@32 level (80.00) and save 25.25% and 21.43% of tokens, whereas the selected thresholds save 42.58% and 38.92% with a higher macro score. Our defaults thus sit at the low-saving end of the grid rather than at the calibrated optimum, which suggests that the gains in Section 5.2 do not rely on a favorable choice of δ \delta .

blocks.en: The framework of StepBack does not fix how the rollback point is chosen. For a given allocation ( n d , n s ) (n_{d},n_{s}) , drafting, suffix resampling, and majority voting are consistent across rules, and only the localization rule Loc \mathrm{Loc} of Section 4 changes. This lets us separate the effect of localization from the effect of reusing prefixes and resampling suffixes. All results in this section use Qwen-3B , the sampling settings of Section 5.1 , and B = 32 B=32 answers per question.

We keep only their rule for choosing that step, compute it with the same PRM as PRM-signal ( Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B ), and leave the rest of StepBack unchanged. • Min-advantage is inspired by Singh et al. [2025] . blocks.en: Table 8 compares all rules at ( n d , n s ) = ( 16 , 2 ) (n_{d},n_{s})=(16,2) over the 4,166 questions of Table 2 . First, every rule saves tokens relative to SC@32 (5.29–44.07%) while staying within 0.25 points of its accuracy. This suggests that much of the token saving in StepBack comes from reusing prefixes and resampling suffixes, regardless of the rollback rule. Second, rules that roll back late are strong efficiency baselines: Fixed -75% and Final-step are 0.05 points above SC@32 while saving 33.66% and 44.07% of tokens. Compared with Final-step , NLL-signal and PRM-signal improve accuracy by only 0.07 and 0.12 percentage points, respectively. Their token-saving rates are 19.51 and 27.11 percentage points lower, respectively. Third, the two signals reach the highest accuracy among all rules. NLL-signal is above Random , Fixed -25%, Fixed -50%, Min-advantage , and Absolute-PRM on both accuracy and saving. Among the PRM-based rules, PRM-signal is above Min-advantage on both axes ( + 0.41 +0.41 points of accuracy and + 1.15 +1.15 points of saving), and it is 0.12 points more accurate than Absolute-PRM while saving 0.93 points fewer tokens. Unlike Min-advantage , PRM-signal rolls back only when the score drop reaches δ \delta , so drafts without a clear failure keep their whole reasoning chain.

blocks.en: Within StepBack , the rollback rule sets an accuracy–efficiency trade-off rather than having a single best choice. Signal-free late rollback, especially Final-step , gives the largest savings and is the most accurate rule on HotpotQA. Localization signals give the highest pooled accuracy, and with a 7B PRM, the highest MATH500 accuracy, and their benefit is largest when rewritten suffixes dominate the vote. The threshold δ \delta moves each signal along this trade-off, from early rollback toward the Final-step fallback.

blocks.en: 1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The abstract and introduction summarize the main contribution of StepBack as an error-localized suffix resampling method for efficient test-time reasoning. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We discuss limitations in Section 8 . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not present formal theoretical results such as theorems or lemmas. We include only analytical discussions to provide intuition for the proposed method. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Section 5 describes the evaluated datasets, models, decoding hyperparameters, sample budgets, voting procedure, and evaluation metrics needed to reproduce the main results. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We use publicly available benchmarks and open-source model checkpoints. We provide a GitHub repository with the implementation and reproduction instructions. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We specify the experimental setup and implementation details in Section 5.1 . We provide hyperparameters for methods in Section J . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: In Appendix K , we use different random seeds to do the experiments on the MATH 500 dataset. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: In Section 5.1 , we provide implementation details. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The research uses publicly available datasets and model checkpoints, does not involve private user data or human-subject experiments, and conforms to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. We preserve anonymity in the submission and report potential societal impacts and limitations. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We discuss broader impacts in Section 8 . StepBack may improve the efficiency and accessibility of reasoning-time inference, but stronger reasoning systems can also be misused or produce more persuasive incorrect outputs; we therefore emphasize careful evaluation and deployment. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not release a new pretrained language model, image generator, scraped dataset, or other high-risk asset. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We provide credits and license information for the datasets and model checkpoints in Appendix I , and use them only for research evaluation. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not introduce a new dataset, model checkpoint, or benchmark asset. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not involve crowdsourcing experiments or human-subject studies. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? We describe the backbone models, PRM scoring models, and any LLM-assisted error annotation or analysis protocol in Section 5 and B . blocks.zh: 一、导 言 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 抽象和介绍总结了StepBack的主要贡献,它是用于高效测试时间推理的一种错误本地化的后缀复标方法. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指摘要和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[否]或[无]答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们讨论第8节的限制。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另辟一个“限制”部分。 文件应说明任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设遭到违反(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)的结果如何有力。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何遭到违反,其影响如何。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果这种办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,这些假设应当加以阐述。 作者应反思影响该办法执行的因素。 例如,一个面部识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像在低光照下拍摄时可能表现不佳. 或语音对文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小来衡量。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的办法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会以完全诚实的限度作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中不承认的限制。 作者应运用最佳判断,承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥着重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚在限制方面的诚实。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[不详]理由: 论文没有提出定理或lemmas等正式的理论结果. 我们只包括分析讨论,以便为拟议方法提供直觉。 准则: • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括理论结果. • 支助 所有论文中的定理,公式和证明,都应该编号,相互参照. • 支助 所有假设都应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在主要论文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证据草图以提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据都应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是] 理由说明:第5节介绍为复制主要结果而需要的经评价的数据集、模型、解码超参数、样本预算、表决程序和评价指标。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或可核查而采取的步骤。 • 根据贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一个具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制这个模型,或者提供对模型的访问. 总论中. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一点的好方法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. • 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交材料都为可复制性提供某种合理的途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当明确说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范结构,文件应清楚、全面地描述这种结构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者描述它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 对于封闭源代码模型,可能以某种方式(如注册用户)限制对模型的获取,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码问题: 文件是否提供了开放的数据和代码,并有足够的指示,如补充材料所述,忠实地复制主要的实验结果? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们使用公开的基准和开放源码模式检查站。 我们提供一个 GitHub 存储器 执行和复制指令。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括需要代码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmission Policy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而拒绝文件,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). • 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何获取原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本,复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从脚本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为保留匿名性,提交人应公布匿名版本(如适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的信息(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(如数据分割、超参数、如何选择、优化者的类型)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们在第5.1节中具体说明试验设置和执行细节。 我们提供了J节方法的超参数。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 实验环境应在文件核心中详细介绍,以便了解结果,使之合理。 详细情况可通过附录中的代码或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告错误是否含有适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:[是] 说明:在附录K中,我们使用不同的随机种子在MATH 500数据集上进行实验. · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有错误栏、信任间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的变异因素(例如,列车/测试拆分、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算错误栏的方法应当加以解释(封闭的表单公式、调用库函数、靴子陷阱等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布错误)。 应明确误差栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准误差. ^ 报告1-西格玛错误栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,提交人最好报告2-西格玛错误栏,而不是说他们有96%的CI。 • 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称误差栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负误差率). • 支助 如果在表格或图中报告错误栏,作者应在文字中解释它们是如何计算的,并在文字中参考相应的数字或表格。 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 理由:在第5.1节中,我们提供执行细节。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额,并估计计算总额。 论文应披露完整的研究项目是否比论文中报告的实验需要更多的计算(例如初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写进论文中). 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复:[是]理由: 研究使用公开的数据集和示范检查站,不涉及私人用户数据或人主体实验,并符合NeurIPS道德守则. 我们在呈件中保持匿名,并报告潜在的社会影响和限制。 • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应该解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和消极社会影响? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们在第8节讨论了更广泛的影响。 StepBack可能会提高推理时间推断的效率和可获取性,但更强大的推理系统也可能被滥用或产生更具有说服力的不正确产出;因此,我们强调认真的评价和部署. · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应当解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件没有涉及社会影响。 • 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(例如:造谣、制造假面貌、监视)、公平考虑(例如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多文件将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以让人们训练出更快生成Deepfake的模型.  • 作者应考虑在技术作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及因(有意或无意)滥用技术而造成的伤害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行封闭释放,在攻击之外提供防御,监测误用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中学习的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布具有高度滥用风险的数据或模型(例如,经过预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或报废数据集)而实施的保障措施? 答复:[不详]理由: 论文没有发布新的预训语言模型,图像生成器,报废数据集,或其他高风险资产. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放的具有高度滥用或双重用途风险的模型,应附带必要的保障措施,允许控制使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制使用该模型或实施安全过滤器。 • 支助 从互联网上拆掉的数据集可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效的保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点,并作出最大的诚意努力。 12. 现有资产的许可证问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有人,是否适当贷记,许可证和使用条款是否明确提及和适当遵守? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们为附录一中的数据集和示范检查站提供信用和许可证信息,仅用于研究评估。 • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应包含每项资产。 • 支助 对于从某一特定来源(如网站)提取的数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 • 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。 13. 新资产问题:文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件? 答复:[不详]理由: 文件没有引入新的数据集、示范检查站或基准资产。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不释放新资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板将数据集/编码/模型的细节作为提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 该文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。 14. 人口集中和人类课题研究 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节? 答复:[不详]理由: 论文不涉及众包实验或人文研究. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。 15. 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)? 答复:[不详]理由: 该文件不涉及众包或人文研究,因此IRB批准不适用. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 视进行研究的国家而定,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在报纸上明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 • 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性(如果适用)的信息,例如进行审查的机构。 16. 关于LLM使用的声明问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作,编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法,科学严谨性或独创性,则不需要声明. 答复:[是] 理由说明: LLMs是研究的核心,因为拟议方法在LLM生成的推理轨迹上运作,并评价推论时间解码行为. 我们描述主干模型,PRM评分模型,以及第5节和B节中任何LLM辅助错误注释或分析协议. · 答案[N/A]是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及任何重要的、原始的或非标准的组成部分。 请参看NeurIPS手册中我们的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations.

blocks.en: Theory assumptions and proofs

blocks.en: Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof?
blocks.zh: 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper does not present formal theoretical results such as theorems or lemmas. We include only analytical discussions to provide intuition for the proposed method.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 论文没有提出定理或lemmas等正式的理论结果. 我们只包括分析讨论,以便为拟议方法提供直觉。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced.

blocks.en: Experimental result reproducibility
blocks.zh: 实验结果可复制

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: Section 5 describes the evaluated datasets, models, decoding hyperparameters, sample budgets, voting procedure, and evaluation metrics needed to reproduce the main results.
blocks.zh: 理由说明:第5节介绍为复制主要结果而需要的经评价的数据集、模型、解码超参数、样本预算、表决程序和评价指标。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.
blocks.zh: · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或可核查而采取的步骤。 • 根据贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一个具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制这个模型,或者提供对模型的访问. 总论中. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一点的好方法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. • 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交材料都为可复制性提供某种合理的途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当明确说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范结构,文件应清楚、全面地描述这种结构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted.

The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. blocks.zh: 我们认识到,提供有效的保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点,并作出最大的诚意努力。

blocks.en: Licenses for existing assets
blocks.zh: 现有资产的许可证

blocks.en: Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected?
blocks.zh: 问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有人,是否适当贷记,许可证和使用条款是否明确提及和适当遵守?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: We provide credits and license information for the datasets and model checkpoints in Appendix I , and use them only for research evaluation.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 我们为附录一中的数据集和示范检查站提供信用和许可证信息,仅用于研究评估。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators.
blocks.zh: • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应包含每项资产。 • 支助 对于从某一特定来源(如网站)提取的数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 • 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。

blocks.en: New assets
blocks.zh: 新资产

blocks.en: Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper does not introduce a new dataset, model checkpoint, or benchmark asset.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 文件没有引入新的数据集、示范检查站或基准资产。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不释放新资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板将数据集/编码/模型的细节作为提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 该文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。

blocks.en: Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects
blocks.zh: 与人类学科的众包和研究

blocks.en: Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)?
blocks.zh: 问题: 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper does not involve crowdsourcing experiments or human-subject studies.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 论文不涉及众包实验或人文研究.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。

blocks.en: Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects
blocks.zh: 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper does not involve crowdsourcing or human-subject research, and therefore IRB approval is not applicable.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 该文件不涉及众包或人文研究,因此IRB批准不适用.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 视进行研究的国家而定,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在报纸上明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 • 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性(如果适用)的信息,例如进行审查的机构。

blocks.en: Declaration of LLM usage
blocks.zh: 声明LLM的使用

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required.
blocks.zh: 问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作,编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法,科学严谨性或独创性,则不需要声明.

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: LLMs are central to the research because the proposed method operates on LLM-generated reasoning trajectories and evaluates inference-time decoding behavior. We describe the backbone models, PRM scoring models, and any LLM-assisted error annotation or analysis protocol in Section 5 and B .
blocks.zh: 理由说明: LLMs是研究的核心,因为拟议方法在LLM生成的推理轨迹上运作,并评价推论时间解码行为. 我们描述主干模型,PRM评分模型,以及第5节和B节中任何LLM辅助错误注释或分析协议.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
